title: A Provision for the Horizon
premise: Bram Vane, who dug for hire across three continents while refusing his famous archaeologist father's name, pulls a sealed chest from a dying river — and inside finds proof that the wreck of the Meridian holds the lost treasury of a nation erased by treaty and theft. The salvage fleet claims salvage law; Bram claims inheritance, because his father spent his final years secretly documenting the drowned kingdom and left Bram the only map that can reach the wreck before the dry season strands it. Racing six tides against the fleet's gunboats, Bram assembles a crew of people the law forgot, uncovers that his father's death was no accident, and must choose between selling the find and restoring it to the descendants of the erased. In the end he beats the fleet by a single tide, surrenders the treasury to the nation's living heirs, and finally signs his own name — Vane, his father's son, and his own digger.
about_author: Lena Brightwater is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways from the Orinoco to the Mekong before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who measure life in miles and find out, too late, that miles were never the unit that mattered.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Is Owed
chapters.summary: Bram Vane, dredging a contracting river for a mining concern, hauls up a bronze-stamped chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: restless competence cracked open by wonder — for the first time in five years, he stops moving.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Bram's old mentor, hydrographer Odile Sarn, calculates the wreck site will be exposed and reachable for only six tides before the dry season drops the river too low. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve as the countdown begins.

chapters.title: The Father Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Among the chest's contents is a survey journal in his estranged father Elias Vane's handwriting — the map to the Meridian's true position. Bram learns Elias died a year ago and left everything to him. POV: Bram, with flashback. Emotional beat: grief he never permitted himself, arriving as anger.

chapters.title: Salvage Law and Other Fictions
chapters.summary: The Corvane Salvage Fleet arrives, claiming river rights; its captain, Ilsa Rehm, offers Bram a finder's fee and a threat in the same sentence. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the cold clarity of realizing the law will not protect what he's found.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Bram recruits people with no legal standing to claim anything: a disgraced Vessian archivist, Nen; a smuggler pilot, Tack; and Odile. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cautious warmth — a crew forming out of shared dispossession.

chapters.title: What the Chest Wouldn't Open
chapters.summary: The chest's inner lock resists all tools; Nen recognizes Vessian funerary work and says it opens only for a descendant's bloodline token — which Elias's journal hints he possessed. POV: Nen. Emotional beat: reverent unease; the past is not passive.

chapters.title: Downstream of the Law
chapters.summary: Tack runs the chest downstream past a Corvane checkpoint in a hair-raising night passage; Bram realizes Rehm wants the chest, not just the wreck. POV: Tack. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with the fear of being hunted.

chapters.title: The Estate of Elias Vane
chapters.summary: Bram breaks into his father's sealed riverside house, finding decades of secret Vessian documentation — and signs someone searched it before him, violently. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the ache of knowing his father only through his absence and his footnotes.

chapters.title: Blood Token
chapters.summary: Bram finds the token: a signet ring Elias wore all his life, which Bram had dismissed as vanity. Nen confirms the Vane line descends from Vessian record-keepers — Elias was heir, and so is Bram. POV: Nen. Emotional beat: identity upended — the name he rejected was a key all along.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Meridian Rises
chapters.summary: The crew reaches the exposed wreck at low water and confirms the treasury hold exists — and that Corvane divers are already cutting toward it from the far side. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into urgency; the race is real now.

chapters.title: Ilsa Rehm's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rehm captures Odile and offers a trade: the wreck for her life, revealing Corvane's client is the treaty government that erased Vessia. POV: Rehm. Emotional beat: her pragmatism fraying — she knows what she's serving and it costs her.

chapters.title: The Exchange at Gray Bend
chapters.summary: Bram trades a forged map for Odile's release, buying a tide but burning trust inside his crew, who suspect he'd have traded the wreck. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: rescued gratitude shadowed by doubt about Bram's heart.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Hold of Names
chapters.summary: Inside the hold, the crew finds not gold first but the Vessian civil registry — the names of every citizen the treaty unpersoned. Nen finds her own family. POV: Nen. Emotional beat: devastation turned to purpose; the treasure is testimony.

chapters.title: The Heirs Downriver
chapters.summary: The crew locates the Vessian diaspora settlement of Karst Hollow, whose elders refuse the registry — accepting it means acknowledging the theft, and the treaty government will come for them. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the bitter discovery that justice has a price the wronged must pay.

chapters.title: Third Tide: Cut Lines
chapters.summary: Corvane divers breach the hold; a submerged knife-fight leaves Tack wounded and a Corvane diver dead, making the crime real on both sides. POV: Tack. Emotional beat: the adventure's romance dies; what remains is stakes.

chapters.title: What Rehm Was Paid
chapters.summary: Bram captures Corvane's paymaster and learns Rehm's client ordered Elias Vane's death — the salvage contract was always about burying the registry. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: rage with a target; grief becomes mission.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Choice of the Ring
chapters.summary: With the blood token, Bram opens the chest's inner chamber: Elias's complete testimony naming the treaty's architects. Bram realizes publishing it will destroy his father's reputation to redeem his name. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: the cost of inheritance made concrete.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Fleet Closes
chapters.summary: Rehm's gunboats trap the crew's barge at the wreck; Rehm, privately sickened by her client, gives Bram one tide's head start — an off-the-books act of justice. POV: Rehm. Emotional beat: her redemption, chosen at the cost of everything she built.

chapters.title: The Long Haul
chapters.summary: A desperate overland portage moves the registry and treasury toward Karst Hollow ahead of the sixth tide and Corvane's last gunboat, through country that wants nothing found in it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into something like devotion.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Wreck Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Climax at the river: the crew, the elders of Karst Hollow, and Corvane's remaining force converge as the final tide exposes the wreck. Bram publicly reads the registry's first page and the treaty testimony as the water rises, forcing witnesses from every side. Rehm turns her guns on her own client's men. Emotional beat: the truth spoken aloud as an act of force no law can undo.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: The treaty government, exposed, negotiates: the treasury and registry pass to Karst Hollow's heirs as legal restitution; Rehm testifies; Corvane collapses. Bram declines reward and standing, asking only that the record bear his name as witness. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet after the flood — justice outside the law becoming law at last.

chapters.title: Miles, and What They Were For
chapters.summary: A year later, Bram teaches at the Karst Hollow archive, the chest open as a monument. He finally reads his father's last unsent letter, forgives him, and measures his life in something other than miles. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: belonging — the horizon no longer something to flee.
